domain: vehicle roadworthiness testing / recurrent inspection outcomes
prediction_question: For a vehicle with at least one completed MOT test, will its next MOT test end in an initial failure (test_result F, or PRS - pass only after rectification at the station) rather than a clean pass, given only what is known up to and including its previous completed test?
prediction_time: The completion instant of the vehicle's previous test (completed_date in the prior test's row). Features are the vehicle's static attributes (make, model, colour, fuel_type, cylinder_capacity, first_use_date, test class) plus its full prior-test history (test dates, intervals, test types including NT/RT, prior results, mileage and mileage deltas, prior defect-item categories from the companion failure-item files). The next test's own fields (test_result, its test_mileage, its completed_date, its defect items) are the label source and never ship as features.
target_definition: Binary from the documented test_result field of the next test: positive if test_result is F or PRS - the DfT/DVSA documented 'initial failure' definition ('Initial failure rate = (Test Fail Results + Test PRS Results) / Total Tests', MOT Testing Data User Guide; the same definition drives the published DVSA/MOT/01 statistical tables). Negative if P. Abandoned/aborted codes (ABR, ABA - measured present at <0.6%) are excluded or handled at construction, to be decided and documented there.

Publisher caveats to carry onto any release, read from the CKAN notes 2026-10-19: 'This data set comes from data held by the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency (DVSA). It is not classed as an official statistic'; the 2018 MOT regime change affected the information presented; the 2017 file was revised in June 2022 to include missing test results.
Vehicle identity is pseudonymised by the publisher (vehicle_id is a pseudonym over registration+VIN) - measured in the row sample; no personal data ships.
split_strategy: Temporal by the NEXT test's year (the label year): train next-tests 2010-2018, eval 2019-2021, holdout 2022-2024; tests 2005-2009 usable only as prior-history priming, never as labelled rows. Measured anchor (2024-08 month prefix, 34,924 rows): initial-fail (F+PRS) 22.1%, clean-pass 77.3%, ABR+ABA 0.55% - both classes amply present every month. Positives cluster by vehicle (19,328 distinct vehicle_ids in the 34,924-row prefix; multiple tests per vehicle per month are normal), so the vehicle is the clustered unit and vehicle_id must NOT be the runner id column: the row id is the unique next-test key, prior-history features are precomputed at construction, and the raw vehicle pseudonym ships only as a declared high-cardinality column if at all.

zip_shape_2026_10_19.method: ranged HTTP reads only (zip central directory + partial member decompression; ~14 ranged requests, ~4.5 MB transferred for the whole measurement)
zip_shape_2026_10_19.result: MOT testing data results (2024).zip = 1,531,265,132 bytes compressed (Last-Modified 2025-05-13), 12 monthly members test_result_202401..202412.csv, 7,667,648,876 bytes uncompressed total (per-month 461-746 MB). S3 answers Range requests; construction is a worker job (ESTIMATE: other years are of similar per-year size - only 2024 was measured).

measurements.row_schema_2026_10_19: Header of test_result_202408.csv, verbatim: test_id,vehicle_id,test_date,test_class_id,test_type,test_result,test_mileage,postcode_area,make,model,colour,fuel_type,cylinder_capacity,first_use_date,completed_date. Sample row: 982603987,596187188,2024-08-19,4,NT,P,65494.0,HG,BENTLEY,CONTINENTAL,SILVER,PE,5998,2006-03-01,2024-08-19T14:10:35.000Z
measurements.key_uniqueness_warning_measured: test_id is NOT unique: 6,336 test_id values appear more than once within the one-month prefix (top test_id 1934795005 appears 36 times; the file's first two rows are byte-identical). Construction must define a total order and dedup explicitly - keying or paging on test_id alone would repeat or drop rows.
measurements.cross_check_against_published_summary_pr: Prefix initial-fail 22.1% / final-fail 17.7% (August 2024, all classes, predominantly class 4) against the publisher's DVSA/MOT/01: FY2025-26 classes 3&4 initial 27.51% / final 22.30%, classes 1&2 13.40%, class 7 34.00%. Same magnitude and class ordering (August is a historically lenient month and the prefix mixes classes); no contradiction.
measurements.extraction_cost: Measured on the coordinator class: the whole shape measurement was ~14 ranged requests / ~4.5 MB / seconds. Construction is worker-scale: 1.53 GB compressed per year (2024 measured; other years labelled estimates) and ~7.7 GB uncompressed per year, so a 2010-2024 build is roughly 23 GB download and ~115 GB uncompressed processing - ESTIMATE derived from the single measured year; re-measure one more year on the worker before committing to the full window. Bounding to class 4 plus adjacent classes cuts this sharply.

next_action: GO to construction (advancement session owns it). Construction step: on a worker, download per-year results and failure-item zips for the chosen window (2010-2024), sort by (vehicle_id, test_date, completed_date) for a total order and dedup explicitly (test_id repeats are measured), join each vehicle's consecutive tests, label next-test initial-fail (F/PRS positive, P negative, ABR/ABA resolved and documented), features strictly from the previous test and earlier (static vehicle attributes + history including mileage deltas and prior defect categories from the item files), exclude every next-test field and its defect items from the shipped columns, freeze train next-year 2010-2018 / eval 2019-2021 / holdout 2022-2024, declare vehicle_id as high-cardinality (never the runner id column; row id = unique next-test key), pin the DVSA/MOT/01 aggregate rates as the cross-check fixture, then run the qualification gate on the worker over the full artifact.

novelty_check.theirs: The raw per-year DVSA/DfT anonymised MOT files (open, OGL); a personal GitHub EDA with a 2-feature SGD pass/fail experiment on one year/postcode/class (adin786/mot-data, 76% acc); a commercial MOT-failure predictor (Lisense) built on DVSA history; the publisher's own aggregate fail-rate tables (DVSA/MOT/01)
novelty_check.ours: Full-history next-MOT-test outcome prediction: prior-test history features (results, mileage deltas, defect categories from the failure-item files) plus static vehicle attributes, frozen temporal splits (next-test years 2010-2018/2019-2021/2022-2024), leakage-disciplined shipped columns, scored runner contract for coding-agent evals
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
